intervals.label: installation and commissioning
intervals.note: Year precision. The review says the detector was commissioned in 1982; the collaboration's own paper says continuous data taking began on 19 February 1984 with 240 t and that the full 912 t was reached in June 1985. The end of this interval is the start of continuous data taking. The detector grew module by module, so installation overlapped data taking.
intervals.quote: The excavation started in 1979 and the first experiment - a 900 ton iron tracking calorimeter to search for proton decay (“Frejus experiment”) - was commissioned in 1982.

intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: Day precision, from the collaboration's own paper. Mass 240 t at the start, 912 t from June 1985. The quote is three consecutive sentences of that section.
intervals.quote: Continuous data taking started February 19, 1984 with a mass of 240 tons. The size of the detector was gradually increased until the final mass of 912 tons was reached in June 1985. Data taking ended September 13, 1988.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: end of data taking.

placements.note: The paper places the detector in the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane but gives no hall coordinate; the site record is the laboratory's own approximate point.
placements.quote: It was located in the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane in the Alps and consisted of flash tubes for tracking and Geiger tubes for triggering.

fiducial_mass.quote: This reduces the fiducial mass to 700 tons leading to an exposure of 2.0 kiloton year (kty).

total_mass.quote: The size of the detector was gradually increased until the final mass of 912 tons was reached in June 1985.

summary.plain: A stack of thin iron plates alternating with gas-filled flash chambers that photograph the tracks of charged particles from two angles, about 900 tons in all, installed deep inside the Fréjus road-tunnel mountain.
summary.technical: Tracking calorimeter: 912 flash-chamber planes (5 mm x 5 mm cells) between 3 mm iron plates, with 113 planes of Geiger tubes (15 mm cells) giving a trigger of grouped hits in about 1 m^3 (threshold about 200 MeV); cells alternate vertical and horizontal for two orthogonal views.

technology.quote: The fine granularity of this 900 ton tracking calorimeter is achieved by a sandwich structure consisting of 912 flash chambers (5 mm × 5 mm cells) and iron ( 3 mm) planes
technology.value: Modular iron-plate tracking calorimeter with plastic flash chambers (5 mm cells) and Geiger-tube trigger planes
